solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Group of eight taking time in old grotto

indicators.note: the grotto word takes in the time letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a grotto is a cave

explanation.surface: A band of eight people sets aside time in an ancient grotto.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a span of eight notes forms one set, and the word also names any group of eight, such as verse lines.

clue.text: Not many supporting scoundrel in travel restriction

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece supporting another sits below it

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man, a scoundrel
not many means few

explanation.surface: A handful of people back a rogue under a ban on movement.
explanation.definitionFit: An order keeping people indoors at set hours restricts their movement about town.

clue.text: One sent letter in area with Don feeding Dee

indicators.note: one piece feeding another goes into it

parts.note: taken as written: the name of a river
to don clothes is to dress

explanation.surface: Someone receives a letter in a district where a man called Don feeds a man called Dee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a name but is the verb meaning put on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: The person to whom mail is directed is its recipient, the one it is sent to.

clue.text: Irritation right in retina that needs treatment

indicators.note: the agreement word goes in among the reworked eye letters
letters that need treatment must be worked over and rearranged

parts.note: 'Right!' as an exclamation of assent means yes

explanation.surface: A patient has a sore spot in the retina that a doctor must treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that needs treatment' makes ETRAIN, and 'in' puts the assent word after its first E. 'Right!' said in agreement is the yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Overworked eyes become sore and tired, a kind of irritation from too much close reading.

clue.text: Courage shown in personal column?

definitions.meaning: the spinal column every person carries, playing on a newspaper's personal ads column

explanation.definitionFit: Grit is called this figuratively, and literally it is the spine, a column of bones inside each person.

clue.text: Fabric is held in short wooden strip

indicators.note: the small word is held inside the cut-down strip
short means the strip word loses its last letter

parts.note: a batten is a long thin strip of wood

explanation.surface: Some cloth is pinned to a stubby length of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' leaves BATTE, and 'held in' places the small word between its two Ts.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fine light cotton or linen cloth, a type of fabric.

clue.text: Hard to be expelled from immaculate social group

indicators.note: the hard letter is thrown out of the pure word

parts.note: immaculate means pure, chaste
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A tough type is thrown out of a spotless social set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be expelled from' removes H from CHASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu society a hereditary class is one fixed social rank, hence any exclusive social group.

clue.text: Courageous Victor breaking into Bank of Scotland

indicators.note: the radio letter breaks into the hillside word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a brae is a Scots word for a hillside or bank
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A daring man named Victor burgles a famous Scottish bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank of Scotland' is not the bank but a Scottish slope: BRAE, as in Scots songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bold and fearless are synonyms of each other, describing someone who faces danger.

clue.text: Get iron transmuted to new element

indicators.note: transmuted means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An alchemist turns iron into a brand-new element.
explanation.definitionFit: This colourless gas, symbol N, is a chemical element making up most of the air.

clue.text: Peter out in allotment finds incline

indicators.note: the fading word goes in the middle of the allowance word

parts.note: a grant is an allotment, a sum allotted
to peter out is to fade away, to die

explanation.surface: Peter leaves his garden allotment and discovers it is on a slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter out' reads as a man leaving, but it is the phrase meaning die away.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope's steepness, and the slope itself, is called this, as with a road rising uphill.

clue.text: Work in texting service is painful

indicators.note: the creative word goes in the middle of the messaging letters

parts.note: SMS is the short message service used for texts
a work of art: art means creative work

explanation.surface: Tapping out messages on a phone can hurt your thumbs.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means stings or hurts, as a cut does.

clue.text: Really dislike exam after two low grades

indicators.note: the exam word comes after the grades

parts.note: D and E are two low marks in school grading
an exam is a test

explanation.surface: A student hates the exam after scoring two poor marks.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe or abhor something is to dislike it intensely.

clue.text: Poet retaining English structure as basis

indicators.note: the poet's name retains the English letter inside it

parts.note: John Skelton was a Tudor English poet

explanation.surface: A poet keeps English verse forms as the foundation of his work.
explanation.definitionFit: A bare framework on which something is built is its basic outline, like a bony frame.

clue.text: Bluejay appearing regularly in meadow

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the bird's name

explanation.surface: A blue bird is often seen in a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for a grassy field, pasture or meadow.

clue.text: Musical performer doubly caddish?

definitions.meaning: a piper who entertains by playing to serpents
a snake and a charmer are both caddish types, so the man is two cads in one

explanation.definitionFit: A street entertainer who plays a pipe to coax serpents is a performing musician of a sort.

clue.text: Morals hit badly when Sky drops The Stones?

indicators.note: badly means the letters are put together wrongly, rearranged

explanation.surface: Moral standards suffer when a broadcaster cancels a Rolling Stones show.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky reads as the TV company and The Stones as the band; really ice stones fall from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Pellets of ice dropping from clouds are called hailstones, so the weather event is the sky dropping them.

clue.text: Tutor in break makes check

indicators.note: the teaching word goes in the pause word

parts.note: a break is a rest
to tutor is to train

explanation.surface: A tutor during a break has to rein himself in.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding back or curbing something is to keep it in check, a noun sense of control.

clue.text: Educated to use repetition following lecturer's lead

indicators.note: the repeating word follows the lecturer's first letter
a lead is the first letter of the word lecturer's

parts.note: to iterate is to repeat, to use repetition

explanation.surface: An educated speaker repeats points, copying the lecturer's style.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone able to read and write well, or cultured, counts as educated.

clue.text: Sedation abused during fights in sick films

indicators.note: the reworked letters come during the contest word, inside it

parts.note: vies means competes, fights

indicators.note: abused means mistreated, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sedatives are misused during brawls in a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abused' makes DEONASTI, which 'during' places after the first two letters of the fights word. 'sick' means sickening, not ill.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the 1980s British label for gory horror videotapes, which are sickening movies.

clue.text: Creature from Old World lakes originally

indicators.note: originally points to the initial letters of the three words

explanation.surface: An animal comes from the lakes of Europe and Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: This night bird is one example of a creature.

clue.text: Tower viewed in modified telescope firm put out

indicators.note: modified means altered, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the company letters are put out of the instrument word

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A tower is seen through a telescope altered by the firm that made it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' removes CO from TELESCOPE, leaving TELESPE, which 'modified' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A church spire rising from a tower, or the tower itself, is this structure.

clue.text: Persian for one using iron railway

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a railway is a line

explanation.surface: A Persian traveller makes use of an iron railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Persian' suggests a person from Iran, but here it is the long-haired cat breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A Persian is a breed of cat, so it is an example of a cat-family animal.

clue.text: Model and casual worker behind schedule

parts.note: a temp is a temporary, casual worker
behind schedule means late

explanation.surface: A model and an agency worker both arrive late for the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern or guide shape used to make copies is a model for them.

clue.text: Artwork for King or Queen

definitions.meaning: a single work of art, as in a museum's prize exhibit
a chessman, such as the king or queen

explanation.definitionFit: A painting is called a work or item of art, and chessmen are each called this.

clue.text: Ship loads drink that's brought back strength

indicators.note: the reversed drink loads the ship letters into itself
brought back means the drink word is turned round

parts.note: tea is a drink
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A vessel takes on board a drink that restores its crew's vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's brought back' gives AET, and 'loads' puts the steamship letters between its A and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong point or valuable quality is a strength in someone's favour.

clue.text: Dreadful setter in the way

indicators.note: dreadful means awful, so the letters are badly arranged

explanation.surface: A terrible crossword compiler is causing an obstruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A road in a town, as in a street name ending in Way, is a public way.

clue.text: Irritant gas about Mars causing stroke

indicators.note: the tear-gas letters go about the war god, around him

parts.note: CS gas is a riot-control irritant
Ares is the Greek counterpart of Mars, god of war

explanation.surface: A noxious gas surrounding the planet Mars leads to a medical stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: Mars is the Roman war god, not the planet; his Greek equivalent is ARES.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle touch with the hand is a stroke, as in a fond pat.

clue.text: Greek character's piece about men reversing ban

indicators.note: the letter and piece go about the reversed soldiers, around them

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: reversing means the soldiers' letters are turned round

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers or men
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: A Greek man's bit about his men making a U-turn on a ban.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns the soldiers into a pair that 'about' sets just after the first letter of the Greek character.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbid something by rule or law is to ban it.

clue.text: Write article on nearly-new drug

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another comes after it
nearly means the word new loses its final letter

parts.note: to pen is to write
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Pen a feature on an almost-new medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops the last letter of new; 'on' puts the writing and article words after that stub.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer's Odyssey this was a potion that banished grief, so a drug of forgetfulness.

clue.text: Mother drinking Tango becomes issue

indicators.note: the mother word drinks the dance letter, taking it inside

parts.note: mater is Latin for mother, old school slang for one's mum
Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Mum's habit of drinking a Tango, a fizzy orange, becomes a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: Tango is a British fizzy orange drink; here it is the radio code word for T.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject or question under discussion is an issue or affair, a thing to be dealt with.
